student.why_not_alt: On d2 the queen is attacked by the b7-bishop and must move with the rook. After 1...Re8 2.f4 d6 3.cxd6 cxd6, White has no follow-up and the game is equal.
student.plan: Castle, then use the queen and rooks against Black's queenside pawns.

teacher.assessment: White is winning by force: the black king on h5 is boxed in, and Be2 is checkmate.
teacher.idea: Check the trapped king along the open diagonal; every escape square is already covered.
teacher.why_best: Be2+ hits h5 along e2-f3-g4. Nf5 covers h4 and h6, the f4-pawn covers g5, the bishop covers g4, and g6 is Black's own pawn. Black cannot block or capture, so it is mate.
teacher.why_not_alt: Rb6 still wins material, but it lets the king escape with Kg4 and Kf3, turning instant mate into a long endgame.
teacher.plan: Deliver mate immediately with Be2#.

student.idea: Be2# is a forced mate: the bishop checks along the diagonal toward the king.
student.assessment: White is winning. Black's king is stuck in the centre, and White's pieces are aimed at it.
student.why_best: Be2# is a mating attack. The bishop on e2 covers f5 and h5, and the rook on b8 attacks the king. After 1...Kg4 2.Ne3+ Kf3 3.Rxb8, White wins the rook outright and the king is mated.
student.why_not_alt: Rb6 is a slow development move. It ignores the mate threat and lets Black play 1...Kg4, so White stays a piece up but never wins the game.
student.plan: Play Be2# and win the rook outright; the king is mated.

teacher.assessment: Roughly equal. White's rooks press down the g-file, but Black's position holds if the king steps aside safely.
teacher.idea: Get off the g-file and the bishop's diagonal, then trade the c4-bishop.
teacher.why_best: On h8 the king is off the open g-file, and f7 is no longer pinned. Black can follow with Ne6 to trade off White's strong bishop: 2.Rg3 Ne6 3.Bxe6 fxe6, with a compact pawn structure.
teacher.why_not_alt: Kf8 walks toward the centre. After Rg3, Rdg1 and the f4 break, White opens more lines and Black's pawns end up split into isolated targets.
teacher.plan: Play Ne6 to trade the bishop, then use the rooks to contest the g-file.

student.idea: Step out of check onto h8, where White's pieces can't reach it.
student.assessment: Roughly equal. Black's king is in check, and White's pieces are aimed at it.
student.why_best: On h8 the king is safe from rook, bishop and knight. After 2.Rg3 Ne6 3.Bxe6 fxe6, Black's pawns become isolated, and the e5 pawn stays a target.
student.why_not_alt: On f8 the king faces the g3 rook and the c4 bishop. After 2.Rg3 Re8 3.Rdg1, White's pieces swarm in, and Black's pawns become doubled.
student.plan: Play Ne6, then use the e5 pawn and the a7 pawn against White's king.

teacher.assessment: Black is winning: White is in check and the queen on d8 hangs to Re8, so material will be lost.
teacher.idea: You're in check and losing the queen anyway, so capture the checking rook now.
teacher.why_best: 1.Bxc1 removes the rook at once. After 1...Nxe2+ 2.Kf2 Rxd8 3.Kxe2, White also wins back the knight, keeping the loss as small as possible.
teacher.why_not_alt: 1.Kf2 lets Black take the queen first with 1...Rxd8. Black then grabs the e2 bishop with the knight and it escapes, so White ends up much further behind.
teacher.novel_concept: damage control: when losing material, grab the most you can
teacher.plan: Recapture the knight with the king, then use the active king and bishop to resist.

student.idea: Take the checking rook, then trade into a winning endgame.
student.assessment: Black is winning. White's king is in the centre and the d4-rook is giving checks.
student.why_best: 1.Bxc1 removes the rook that is giving checks. After 1...Nxe2+ 2.Kf2, White has traded off the bishop pair. White's king is stuck in the centre, and Black's pieces are active.
student.why_not_alt: 1.Kf2 ignores the rook. After 1...Rxd8 2.Bxc1, White has traded rooks but still has the bishop pair. Black's pieces stay active, and White's king is stuck in the centre.
student.plan: Trade pieces, centralise the king, and convert the extra material.

teacher.assessment: White is better with an extra exchange for a pawn, but Black's queen and knights are eyeing White's king.
teacher.idea: Offer the queen trade on g3 to kill Black's kingside attack.
teacher.why_best: Qg3 blocks the b8–h2 diagonal and offers a trade. After 1...Qxg3+ 2.hxg3 Black has no attack left. White's material edge and the rook on the seventh then decide the endgame, even if Black wins g4.
teacher.why_not_alt: Qf3 keeps queens on, so White's king stays a worry. The rook has to leave the seventh rank, and Black gets time to regroup with Rc7, Qc8 and Ne5.
teacher.plan: Trade queens, keep the rook active on the seventh, then convert the material edge.

student.idea: Give the queen a central post to hit the kingside and the c8 rook.
student.assessment: White is better: the queen and rook are active, Black's king is stuck in the centre and White's pieces are aimed at it.
student.why_best: Qg3 eyes the c8 rook and the g6 knight. After 1...Qxg3+ 2.hxg3, White has a rook on the seventh and a knight on g6. The queen also eyes the f8 bishop and the h2 pawn.
student.why_not_alt: Qf3 is too slow. Black gets time to regroup with ...Rc7 and ...Ne5, and White's pieces stay passive.
student.plan: Bring the rook to b7, then use the queen and knight against Black's king.

teacher.assessment: White is clearly better: a tempo on the queen creates a protected passed c-pawn, and White controls the d-file.
teacher.idea: Hit the queen with tempo, then push c5 for a protected passer.
teacher.why_best: 1.b4 attacks the queen, so Black has no time to fight back. After 1...Qc7 2.c5, the c-pawn is passed and guarded by b4. It cramps Black and gives White a long-term trump.
teacher.why_not_alt: 1.Be2 just guards c4 passively. Black plays ...a5 and ...b4, dissolves White's queenside majority and equalises. White never gets a passed pawn.
teacher.plan: Support the c5 passer, keep control of the d-file, and push the pawn.

student.idea: Push b4 to hit the queen and the c5 pawn at once.
student.assessment: White is clearly better: Black's queen and c5 pawn are loose, and White can win a pawn.
student.why_best: 1.b4 attacks both the queen and the c5 pawn. After 1...Qc7 2.c5, White wins a pawn and keeps the extra material. White's rook then eyes d1, and White's pieces become active.
student.why_not_alt: 1.Be2 is a passive retreat. Black plays a5 and b4, and White's pieces stay cramped. The extra pawn is gone and the position is equal.
student.plan: Win the b-pawn, then use the rook and pieces against Black's king.

teacher.assessment: Roughly equal after Rxd5. White is down material but Black's boxed-in king on g8 gives White counterplay.
teacher.idea: Take the bishop, then use Black's weak back rank to force queen trades.
teacher.why_best: 1.Rxd5 wins a whole piece. After 1...Qxf2 2.Rxe5, Re8 threatens mate because the h8 rook traps Black's king. Black must give up the queen with 2...Qxf1+ 3.Re1 Qxe1+ 4.Bxe1, and White stays slightly ahead.
teacher.why_not_alt: Nc8 is too slow. Black grabs f2 and keeps the queen on White's second rank. Black can even get a mate-in-one chance, and wins the material race.
teacher.plan: Trade off Black's queen, then use your extra minor pieces against the rook.

student.idea: Take the undefended bishop on d5, then trade queens to end Black's attack.
student.assessment: Roughly equal after Rxd5. White wins back the piece, and Black's attack on f2 is gone.
student.why_best: The d5 bishop has no defender. 1.Rxd5 removes it from Black's attack. After 2.Rxe5 White has traded queens, so Black's rook no longer reaches the seventh rank. White is ahead in material and the attack is gone.
student.why_not_alt: 1.Nc8 lets Black play 1...g6. The knight escapes with tempo, and Black's queen and rook stay active. White stays a piece down and is slightly worse.
student.plan: Trade queens, then use the extra material and the bishop pair against Black's pawns.

teacher.assessment: Black is slightly better. The extra pawn counts, but Black's king is stuck in the centre and must get safe.
teacher.idea: Fork queen and rook with tempo, chasing the queen off f7 before castling.
teacher.why_best: 1...Nd2 attacks Qb3 and Rf1 at once. White must spend moves: 2.Qb4 then Rfe1. The queen leaves the b3-f7 diagonal, so Black castles queenside and keeps the extra pawn.
teacher.why_not_alt: 1...O-O-O lets White's queen stay active. After 2.Qc4+ Qc6 3.Qxf7 White wins back the pawn, and the position is equal.
teacher.plan: Castle queenside, put a rook on the d-file and hold onto the extra pawn.

student.idea: Block the f7 pawn with a knight, then castle and finish development.
student.assessment: Black is slightly better: an extra pawn, and White's king is still in the centre with no castling.
student.why_best: 1...Nd2 attacks the f7 pawn, so White must defend it. After 2.Qb4 O-O-O Black is castled and the knight sits on a strong central square. White's king stays in the centre, and Black's queen and rooks are active.
student.why_not_alt: 1...O-O-O is too slow. White plays 2.Qc4+ and forks the queen and rook, winning a pawn. Black's knight is stuck on d2, and the position is equal.
student.plan: Castle, then use the queen and rooks against White's king and queenside pawns.

teacher.assessment: White is winning: Black's king sits on a weak back rank and the a2-g8 diagonal, and Black's pieces are loose.
teacher.idea: Pin the f7-rook to the king, then use the back rank to win the queen.
teacher.why_best: After 1.Nxf7 Rxf7 the rook is pinned by Qd5. Then 2.Ra8! attacks the queen, and Black's back rank is weak. After Qxa8 Qxa8+ White wins queen for rook and keeps a pinned rook and passed centre pawns.
teacher.why_not_alt: 1.Nc6 hits the queen and bishop, but Black simply moves the queen. White keeps pressure without cashing in. No pin, no back-rank combination, no extra queen.
teacher.plan: Keep the pinned f7-rook tied down and push the passed central pawns.

student.idea: Take the pawn on f7. The knight is lost anyway, so grab it first.
student.assessment: White is winning. The f7 pawn is loose, and taking it leaves White a full piece up.
student.why_best: 1.Nxf7 Rxf7 removes the knight, so White is a full piece up. After 2.Ra8 Qxa8 3.Qxa8+ White has won the exchange and is a clear piece up.
student.why_not_alt: 1.Nc6 is a slow, passive move. Black gets time to save the knight with Qe8 and Bf6, and White stays only a pawn up.
student.plan: Collect the f7 pawn, then use the extra piece and queen to convert.

teacher.assessment: Black is better thanks to an extra piece, but White has real counterplay against f6 and the black king.
teacher.idea: Get the king off the g1-a7 diagonal and the f-file, keeping the attack going.
teacher.why_best: On h1 the king is off both of Black's attacking lines, so White can keep attacking. After 1...Qd7 2.g6 h5 3.Bxf6+ Rxf6 4.Qxf6+, the a1-bishop and the queen win back the material.
teacher.why_not_alt: Kf1 puts the king on the f-file facing the f8-rook. Black gets ...Qf5+ with tempo, White is forced into Be2 and Qf2, and Black trades queens a piece up.
teacher.plan: Push g6 and use Ba1 and Qh4 to break open f6 against the black king.

student.idea: Step off the e3–f6 diagonal and keep the king near the centre.
student.assessment: Black is better: White's king is stuck on h1, and Black's queen and bishop are aimed at it.
student.why_best: Kh1 moves the king off the e3–f6 diagonal, so Black's queen and bishop no longer hit it. White can then play g6 to open lines toward Black's king, and the queen stays active.
student.why_not_alt: Kf1 leaves the king on f1, where the queen and bishop aim. After Qd7 and Qf5+, White has to give up the queen for a bishop, and Black is winning.
student.plan: Play g6, then use the queen and bishop to harass Black's king.

teacher.assessment: Black is winning with extra material. The only issue is the knight on d4, attacked by Bb2 and Rd1.
teacher.idea: Capture with the threatened piece: the knight saves itself by taking a bishop.
teacher.why_best: 1...Nxb5 grabs a whole bishop and gets the loose knight out of danger in one move. White's rook must retreat (2.Rd7), then ...d4 blunts the b2-bishop. Black stays a clean piece up.
teacher.why_not_alt: 1...Bxe7 wins the rook, but 2.Bxd4 takes the knight back. That nets only the exchange instead of a full piece, and White keeps the bishop pair.
teacher.plan: Blunt Bb2 with ...d4, trade rooks on the d-file, and convert the extra piece.

student.idea: Recapture with the knight so it guards d4 and the e7 rook.
student.assessment: Black is winning. The d4 knight is attacked twice, and the e7 rook is attacked once, so recapturing is essential.
student.why_best: 1...Nxb5 wins the piece back and keeps the knight on d4, where it protects the e7 rook. After 2.Rd7 d4, Black's rook and knight are active and White's king is stuck in the centre.
student.why_not_alt: 1...Bxe7 grabs a rook but leaves the d4 knight undefended. After 2.Bxd4, White wins the piece back and the d4 knight is gone, so Black's edge shrinks to a small one.
student.plan: Play ...d4, then ...Rad8 to activate the rook and keep the knight on d4.

teacher.assessment: Black is slightly better: the attacked rook escapes with tempo, letting Black win back the loose b5 bishop.
teacher.idea: Save the attacked rook while attacking the g7 bishop.
teacher.why_best: Bg7 attacks the h8 rook, and Black's Ra5 already eyes the loose bishop on b5. 1...Rg8 hits the g7 bishop, so White must spend a move on it (2.Bd4). Then 2...Rxb5 cleans up and Black stands slightly better.
teacher.why_not_alt: 1...Re8 saves the rook but threatens nothing. White gets a free move (2.Ke2), and the trades that follow end with White recapturing on a2 and standing clearly better.
teacher.plan: Take b5, then use your active rooks and bishops against White's d6 pawn.

student.idea: Save the attacked rook by moving it to g8, where it eyes the h8 rook.
student.assessment: Black is slightly better: White's rook on h8 is attacked by the g4-bishop, and Black's rook can hit it.
student.why_best: The b5-bishop attacks the h8-rook. Rg8 escapes it and eyes it. After 2.Bd4 Rxb5 3.Rxa2, Black wins the a2-knight and the b5-bishop, and the material edge holds.
student.why_not_alt: Re8 saves the rook but leaves it on e4. After 3.Nxe4 Rxe4, White wins the e4-knight and the exchange, and White is clearly better.
student.plan: Win the b5-bishop, then trade pieces to convert the material edge.

teacher.assessment: Black is better: White's bishop on f7 has wandered deep into Black's camp and can be cut off.
teacher.idea: Play ...e6 to shut the f7-bishop's escape route and trap it.
teacher.why_best: After ...e6 the bishop has no safe square. e8 is covered by the king, g8 by the rook, e6 by the c8-bishop and g6 by the h7-pawn. Black rounds it up with ...Rf8 and ...Rxf7, winning material and undoubling the e-pawns.
teacher.why_not_alt: 1...Kc7 lets the bishop escape with Bb3. Black is left with doubled, isolated pawns and nothing to show for them, so White is slightly better.
teacher.plan: Collect the f7-bishop with ...Rf8 and ...Rxf7, then use the extra piece.

student.idea: Push e6 to open the f7-bishop's diagonal toward f2.
student.assessment: Black is slightly better: White's f7-bishop is stuck in the centre and can be taken for free.
student.why_best: 1...e6 opens the f7-bishop's diagonal toward f2. After 2.Bg5 Rf8 3.Ne4 Rxf7, Black wins the piece back and the f7-bishop is gone. White's f-pawn is also broken.
student.why_not_alt: 1...Kc7 is too slow. White calmly plays 2.Bb3 and keeps the extra space, and Black's king stays in the centre.
student.plan: Win the f7-bishop, then use the extra space and the queenside majority.

teacher.assessment: Equal if Black is accurate. White has more space and a strong e6 pawn, but Black's e5 pawn gives counterplay.
teacher.idea: Centralise the queen, guard e5 and offer the queen trade.
teacher.why_best: Qd4 attacks White's queen and protects e5, so White's queen has no easy target. After 2.Nd5 c6 the queens come off. Black's pawn recaptures to d4 and becomes a passed pawn, which balances White's space.
teacher.why_not_alt: Qh4 goes for a king attack that doesn't land. It leaves e5 loose, so 3.Qxe5 wins a pawn. White also trades queens on f6, reaching an endgame Black shouldn't enjoy.
teacher.plan: Trade queens, then push the d-pawn and blockade e6.

student.idea: Save the attacked queen by hitting the e3 queen, then hit the c3 knight.
student.assessment: Roughly equal. Black's queenside pawns are dangerous, but White's queen and knight are active and threaten checks.
student.why_best: The e5 pawn attacks the queen. 1...Qd4 saves it and attacks the c3 knight. After 2.Nd5 c6 3.Rd1 Nxd5 4.Qxd4 exd4 5.cxd5, Black's queenside pawns become dangerous, and White's queen is attacked.
student.why_not_alt: 1...Qh4 saves the queen passively. After 2.b3 White's queen is centralised, and White's pieces become active. White's pieces then start to hunt Black's queenside pawns.
student.plan: Play ...c6, then ...Nxd5 and ...exd4, and keep the queenside pawns active.

teacher.assessment: Black is winning thanks to the extra bishop, but must get out of check without letting White's rook become active.
teacher.idea: Step the king toward the kingside, behind its pawns and off open files.
teacher.why_best: After 1...Kf8 and ...Kg7 the king is sheltered by f7, f6 and h6. No white rook check lands with tempo, so Black can calmly bring the h8-rook into play (...Rd8) and use the extra piece.
teacher.why_not_alt: 1...Kd8 puts the king on the open d-file. After 2.Bd5 Bxd5 3.Rd1 White's rook wins back time, grabs a5 and creates passed queenside pawns.
teacher.plan: King to g7, rook to the d-file, then push kingside pawns with the extra piece.

student.idea: Step out of check onto the g7 square, where White's pieces are scattered.
student.assessment: Black is winning. White's king is stuck in the centre, and Black's pieces are aimed at it.
student.why_best: On g7 the king is off the a4–h8 diagonal, so White has no tempo. After 2.Re1 Kg7 3.Bb5, White's pieces are scattered and Black's rooks and bishops are aimed at the king.
student.why_not_alt: On d8 the king sits on the a4–h8 diagonal. After 2.Bd5 Bxd5 3.Rd1, White's pieces regroup, and Black's attack is gone.
student.plan: Bring the rook to d8, then use the bishops and queen to hunt the king.

teacher.assessment: White is winning. Black's king is boxed in by its own h8 rook and pawns, and Bh6 covers g7 and f8.
teacher.idea: Force the queen to block, trade it off, then mate on the g-file.
teacher.why_best: 1.Re8+ forces 1...Qf8, since taking the rook loses to a back-rank mate. 2.Rxf8+ removes the queen and keeps the initiative. Then Re3–g3 gives mate because g7 and f8 are covered and h8 is blocked.
teacher.why_not_alt: 1.f4 still wins material and keeps a big edge, but it lets Black breathe. The forced mate against the trapped king disappears.
teacher.plan: Swing the second rook to the g-file for mate while Bh6 seals g7 and f8.

student.idea: Check first, then take the queen. The rook on e8 attacks both.
student.assessment: White is winning. Black's queen on d6 is attacked by the rook and bishop, and White can win it.
student.why_best: 1.Re8+ forces the queen to move. After 1...Qf8 2.Rxf8+ Rxf8, White has a rook on the a-file and the queen on f8. 3.Re3 brings a rook to the third rank, and 4.Rg3# ends the game.
student.why_not_alt: 1.f4 is too slow. Black plays 1...f5, and White's rook on e8 is attacked by the queen. After 2.Re8+ Qf8 3.Bxf8 Rxe8 4.Rxe8 White is down material and the attack is gone.
student.plan: Bring a rook to the third rank, then mate on the g-file.

teacher.assessment: White is winning: an extra exchange and strong pieces closing in on Black's boxed-in king and weak back rank.
teacher.idea: Trade off White's attacking queen with check to kill the mating attack.
teacher.why_best: 1...Qe5+ is check, so White has no time for threats and must trade with 2.Qxe5+ Rxe5. Without queens, the mating danger on the back rank is gone. Black is still worse but keeps playing.
teacher.why_not_alt: 1...Qb2 ignores the back rank. 2.Rf8+ Kg7 3.Rxe8 wins the rook. White's queen and bishop then threaten mate and forks, so Black's position collapses.
teacher.plan: Activate the rook (Ra5-a4), push the a-pawn and hope to hold.

student.idea: Check first, then block with the queen. Don't give up the queen.
student.assessment: White is winning. Black's queen on e2 is attacked twice, and White's queen and rook are aimed at it.
student.why_best: 1...Qe5+ forces 2.Qxe5+ Rxe5. White wins the queen, but the rook stays on e5. Black's queen is still active, and the rook eyes a7. Black can then trade queens and keep fighting.
student.why_not_alt: 1...Qb2 is passive. After 2.Rf8+ Kg7 3.Rxe8, White's rook reaches the seventh and Black's queen is stuck in the centre. White wins the queen and the rook, and the game is over.
student.plan: Trade queens, then use the rook and queen against White's king.

teacher.assessment: Black is clearly better: an extra pawn, a rook already on the second rank, and White's rooks stuck passive.
teacher.idea: Bring the idle rook to the open b-file while the e2-rook stays active.
teacher.why_best: Rb8 activates the f8-rook without giving up anything. The e2-rook keeps its grip on the second rank and the e-file. After 2.Bf3 Rd2 3.Rab1 Rbb2, both Black rooks reach the second rank, and trades only help the side a pawn up.
teacher.why_not_alt: Rb2 moves the active rook off the e-file. White hits back with Bd5 and Re1, so his rooks wake up and he gets counterplay.
teacher.plan: Double rooks on the second rank, trade into a won endgame, and target the weak c4 and a3 pawns.

student.idea: Bring the rook to the second rank to guard the king and the d-file.
student.assessment: Black is better: the rook on b8 guards the king and the d-file, and White's king is stuck in the centre.
student.why_best: Rb8 covers the second rank and the d-file. After 2.Bf3 Rd2, the rook still eyes d1 and the king. White must spend time on Bd5 and Rab1, and Black keeps the extra pawn and active rooks.
student.why_not_alt: Rb2 is passive. White plays Bd5 and Re1, and the rook on b2 is no longer needed. Black's rook is stuck on f8, and White's king gets time to regroup.
student.plan: Keep the rook on b8, keep the extra pawn, and keep White's king in the centre.

teacher.assessment: Equal if Black saves the knight; the c6-knight is attacked twice by the doubled rooks and defended only once.
teacher.idea: Get the knight off the c-file before the doubled rooks win it.
teacher.why_best: On c6 the knight faces two white rooks with only Rc8 guarding it. 1...Ne7 steps off the file. After 2.Rxc8+ Rxc8 Black keeps a rook on the open c-file and material is level.
teacher.why_not_alt: 1...a5 ignores the loose knight. 2.Rxc6 Rxc6 3.Rxc6 simply wins a piece, and the a-pawn is far too slow to matter.
teacher.plan: Trade rooks, hold the c-file, and bring the knight back toward the queenside.

student.idea: Save the attacked knight by retreating it, not by grabbing pawns.
student.assessment: Roughly equal. White threatens Rxc6, but Black can save the knight without falling behind in development.
student.why_best: The c6-knight is attacked by the d4-pawn. Ne7 saves it passively, so Black stays level. After 2.Rxc8+ Rxc8 3.Ra4 Nc6, Black finishes development and the game is roughly equal.
student.why_not_alt: 1...a5 grabs a rook but gives up the knight. After 2.Rxc6 Rxc6 3.Rxc6 a4, White's rook becomes active and White is winning.
student.plan: Finish development, castle, and meet the queen on the c-file.

teacher.assessment: White is slightly better. Black's advanced passers balance it, but the g8 king sits on the bishop's a2-g8 diagonal.
teacher.idea: Step the king off the bishop's diagonal before it opens.
teacher.why_best: The g8 king lines up behind the c4 knight and d5 rook on Bb3's diagonal. 1...Kh8 removes that x-ray. After 2.Rd3 Re2 3.Rxg3 Re1, Black's rooks stay active and the game stays close.
teacher.why_not_alt: 1...Rgf2 leaves the king on the diagonal. After 2.axb5 Rf1 3.Bxc4, White gets discovered-attack chances, and the d2 pawn falls after 5.Kxd2.
teacher.plan: Keep the rooks active against White's king and support the d2 and g3 passers.

student.idea: Step off the g-file and keep the rook on the f8–e2 diagonal.
student.assessment: White is slightly better: the g3 pawn is dangerous, and Black's king is stuck in the centre.
student.why_best: Kh8 escapes the g-file and keeps the rook on the f8–e2 diagonal. After 2.Rd3 Re2 3.Rxg3, Black wins the pawn back and the g3 pawn falls. White's best is 3...Re1, and Black's rook stays active.
student.why_not_alt: Rgf2 leaves the rook off the diagonal. After 2.axb5 Rf1 3.Bxc4, White wins the knight and the exchange, and Black's rook is stuck on the back rank.
student.plan: Win back the g3 pawn, then use the rook and knight against White's queenside.

teacher.assessment: Black is winning: the checking rook on e1 can be captured for a knight, and White's a6-knight is trapped.
teacher.idea: Answer the check by capturing the rook, winning the exchange.
teacher.why_best: Re1 is giving check, and 1...Nxe1 removes it while winning a rook for a knight. After 2.Rxe1+ Kf6, the Na6 has no safe squares. Black's rook controls b8, c7 and c5, so ...Rc6-b6 hunts it down.
teacher.why_not_alt: 1...Kf6 just steps out of check and leaves the rook on e1. White plays Red1, its rooks become active together, and the extra material Black could have won is gone.
teacher.plan: Bring the king to f6, then use ...Rc6-b6 to win the trapped Na6.

student.idea: Take the free rook on e1. The knight is lost anyway.
student.assessment: Black is winning. White's rook on e1 is hanging, and the knight on c2 is lost.
student.why_best: 1...Nxe1 wins a whole rook for a knight. After 2.Rxe1+ Kf6, Black's pieces are active and White's rook is stuck on e1. White's knight on c2 is also lost.
student.why_not_alt: 1...Kf6 is a slow, passive move. It lets White play 2.Red1 and trade pieces, so the extra rook is gone and the position is equal.
student.plan: Activate the knight and bishop, then use the extra rook and the open e-file.

teacher.assessment: White is slightly better despite Black's extra material: the white queen and central pawns are active, Black's pieces are uncoordinated.
teacher.idea: Guard the seventh rank and defend the knight before the queen gets in.
teacher.why_best: 1...Rf7 covers the second rank from the side, protects the d7-knight and f6, and frees the bishop to develop. White has no quick queen raid, so the game slows down. Slowing down suits the side with the extra pieces.
teacher.why_not_alt: 1...Kg8 ignores the queen. After 2.Qd6 White grabs c6 and lands on c7, with the queen on the seventh tying Black's pieces up.
teacher.plan: Untangle with Kg8, Nf8 and Bd7, then use the extra pieces against White's pawns.

student.idea: Bring the rook to f7 to guard the kingside and the c8-bishop.
student.assessment: White is slightly better despite Black's extra material, because Black's king is stuck in the centre and White's pieces are active.
student.why_best: Rf7 covers the f-file and the c8-bishop. After 2.g4 Kg8 3.b3 Nf8, Black's rook still eyes g2 and the c8-bishop. White's queen and knight stay active, and Black's pieces stay near the king.
student.why_not_alt: 1...Kg8 leaves the king on the e4-f5 diagonal. After 2.Qd6 Rf7 3.Qxc6, White's queen reaches c7 and the c8-bishop is boxed in. White's pieces then take over.
student.plan: Bring the rook to f7, then use the c8-bishop and knight to harass White's king.

teacher.assessment: White is better. Black's king is stuck in the centre, and White's queen and d5-bishop dominate the light squares.
teacher.idea: Trade off the d5-bishop that stops Black from castling kingside.
teacher.why_best: The d5-bishop covers g8, so Black cannot castle. After 1...Nxd5 2.exd5 Bd7, the bishop on g4 is saved and Black castles soon. White gets a rook to c7, but Black's king finally gets shelter.
teacher.why_not_alt: 1...Bd7 leaves White's strong bishop alive (2.Bb3). Black's king stays stuck in the centre, and the rook goes Rc7-a7 to win the a6 pawn.
teacher.plan: Save the g4-bishop with ...Bd7, castle, then contest the c-file and seventh rank.

student.idea: Trade off White's strong d5 bishop to remove the knight fork threat.
student.assessment: White is better despite Black's extra pawn, because Black's king is stuck in the centre and White's pieces are aimed at it.
student.why_best: The e2 knight forks the g4 bishop. 1...Nxd5 removes that fork. After 2.exd5 the knight is loose, so 2...Bd7 hits the queen and the rook. White's rook then walks to c7 and a7.
student.why_not_alt: 1...Bd7 saves the bishop but leaves the knight forked. After 2.Bb3 g5 3.Rc7 the rook reaches a7, and White's pieces become active.
student.plan: Play ...Bd7, then castle, and keep the knight away from the king.

teacher.assessment: Black is slightly better after winning back the pawn. White's knight on h5 is offside and White's pawns are loose.
teacher.idea: Recapture with the pawn: fix your structure and take g4 away.
teacher.why_best: 1...exf5 gets rid of the backward e6-pawn and gives Black a kingside pawn majority. The f5-pawn covers g4, so White's queen has no active square and plays passively with 2.Kh1 and 3.Qf3.
teacher.why_not_alt: 1...Rxf5 leaves e6 backward and weak. It also lets White's queen use g4 with tempo on the rook (2.Qg4), so White coordinates and holds.
teacher.plan: Use the extra kingside pawn, tie White down, and push ...g6 to drive away the h5 knight.

student.idea: Take the f5 pawn, then trade queens to open the f-file.
student.assessment: Black is slightly better: White's f5 pawn is loose, and Black's rooks and queen can hunt it.
student.why_best: 1...exf5 wins a pawn and removes White's best attacker. After 2.Kh1 Qg6 3.Qf3, the f-file opens toward White's king. Black's queen and rooks then hunt f5, and White's king is stuck in the centre.
student.why_not_alt: 1...Rxf5 grabs a pawn but leaves White's knight on h5. White keeps the extra pawn, and Black's queen and rook stay passive.
student.plan: Bring the queen to g6 and rook to f7, then hunt f5.

teacher.assessment: Black is up a rook, but White can take back at once and level the game.
teacher.idea: Just take the rook on c1: it attacks your rook and wins material back.
teacher.why_best: The c1-rook is loose and is also attacking Re1. 1.Rxc1 removes the attacker and restores material balance. Your rook then sits on the open c-file, and the game is equal.
teacher.why_not_alt: 1.b4 ignores the c1-rook. Black plays Rxe1+ and stays a full rook up. After Qxa4 Black also gets a queenside majority, and White's king is dragged to the centre.
teacher.plan: Use the c-file rook and the strong queen on d6, and push e5 to keep Black passive.

student.idea: Take the rook that attacks your queen, not the one on e1.
student.assessment: Roughly equal. White is a rook down, but Black's queen is exposed and White can pick up material.
student.why_best: The rook on c1 attacks the queen on a5. 1.Rxc1 wins a whole rook for a rook, so material is level. White then plays 2.Qc7 and 3.Qc3, bringing the queen to safety.
student.why_not_alt: 1.b4 ignores the attack. After 1...Rxe1+ 2.Kf2 White has lost the exchange, and Black's queen and rook are active, so White is clearly behind in material.
student.plan: Play 2.Qc7 and 3.Qc3, then castle and use the extra rook.

teacher.assessment: White is winning: the rook on f7 and knight on f6 threaten Rxh7#, and Black's extra material can't fix that.
teacher.idea: Guard h7 and g8 with the queen, even if it costs her.
teacher.why_best: White threatens Rxh7#, since the f6 knight covers h7. 1...Qg8 guards h7 and the king's flight square. Black loses the queen after 2.Ra7 Bb5 3.Nxg8 but avoids mate and keeps fighting.
teacher.why_not_alt: 1...Qa7 offers a trade, but 2.Rxa7 just takes the queen. The rook-and-knight battery on h7 is still there, so Rxh7# follows.
teacher.plan: Survive the mate threats, then use the bishop and pawns to stop the e-pawn.

student.idea: Save the attacked queen by moving it off the h-file, not into a mating net.
student.assessment: White is winning. Black's queen on a8 is attacked by the h7 rook and must move before White's rook reaches h7.
student.why_best: On a8 the queen is attacked by the h7 rook. Qg8 escapes it with a check, so White must act. After 2.Ra7 Bb5 3.Nxg8 Kxg8 4.Ra5 Be8, Black wins the c5 pawn and the queen is safe.
student.why_not_alt: Qa7 gives up the queen for a rook. After 2.Rxa7 d4 3.Rxh7# Black has no queen left, and White wins.
student.plan: Trade queens, then use the queen and knight against White's rook and pawns.

teacher.assessment: Black is winning. The forking knight and active bishops outweigh White's extra material, provided Black keeps the initiative.
teacher.idea: Castle to protect the attacked rook and keep every attacking threat alive.
teacher.why_best: Bc7 threatens the b8 rook. 1...O-O defends it along the back rank and tucks the king away safely. Black keeps the initiative: after 2.Nc3 Nxa1+ the knight takes the rook with check and Black regains the material.
teacher.why_not_alt: 1...Ke7 also covers b8, but it costs a tempo and leaves the king with no pawn cover. 2.Ka4 lets White's king escape, and Black never wins back enough material.
teacher.plan: Take the a1 rook with check, keep checking, and win back material.

student.idea: Castle now. The b4-bishop is loose, so take it.
student.assessment: Black is winning. White's king is stuck in the centre, and Black's pieces are aimed at it.
student.why_best: After 1...O-O the b4-bishop is gone. White's king is stuck in the centre, and Black's pieces are aimed at it. After 2.Nc3 Nxa1+ 3.Ka4 Bc2+ 4.b3 Bxc3, Black wins the exchange and the b8-rook.
student.why_not_alt: 1...Ke7 is slow. White gets time to regroup with 2.Ka4 and 3.Bxb8, and Black's king stays in the centre.
student.plan: Take the b4-bishop, then trade pieces and convert the extra material.

teacher.assessment: Black is somewhat better and up material, but both kings are exposed. White's c4 bishop pins down g8 with discovered checks.
teacher.idea: Run the king to f2, off the h-file, before Black's discovered checks land.
teacher.why_best: On f2 the king escapes the h-file battery. Black has no better than trading queens with 1...Qg3+ 2.Rxg3 Bxg3+ 3.Kxg3. After 3...Rxe4, the discovered check 4.Rf4+ wins material back and leaves a holdable endgame.
teacher.why_not_alt: On h1 the king stays on the h-file under the queen. 1...Bf4+ is a discovered check from h3, and Black's bishop keeps checking with tempo until White's position collapses.
teacher.plan: Get out of the checks, then use the Bc4 and Rf7 discovered checks to regain material.

student.idea: Step out of check onto f2, where Black's queen and rook are still loose.
student.assessment: Black is slightly better: White is in check, and Black's queen and rook are still on the loose.
student.why_best: On f2 the king is no longer trapped. After 1.Kf2 Qg3+ 2.Rxg3 Bxg3+ 3.Kxg3, White has traded queens and bishops, and the rook on f4 becomes active.
student.why_not_alt: Kh1 leaves the king on g8. Black's queen and rook are now very active, and White's king is stuck in the centre with no escape.
student.plan: Trade queens, then use the rook on f4 against Black's queenside pawns.

teacher.assessment: Black is winning. White's king on c2 is exposed to many checks, and White is already a pawn down.
teacher.idea: Don't force anything. Make a quiet move and keep the defenders where they are.
teacher.why_best: Black has 12 checks against the open king, so any forcing try backfires. After 1.g3 Qa1 2.Rb3 Rc8+ 3.Rc3 White trades rooks and only loses the a-pawn, limiting the damage.
teacher.why_not_alt: 1.Qc3 offers a queen trade, but after 1...Qd5 Black hits a2. Then ...Qa2+ and ...Rb3 deflect White's queen, and White loses much more material.
teacher.plan: Keep queen and rook close to the king, block checks, and aim for a fortress.

student.idea: Push the g-pawn to g3 to open the c-file toward Black's king.
student.assessment: Black is winning. White's king on c2 is stuck in the centre, and Black's queen and rook are swarming it.
student.why_best: 1.g3 opens the c-file toward the king. After 1...Qa1 2.Rb3 Rc8+ 3.Rc3, White's rook reaches the c-file and the queen. White's queen and rook are both aimed at Black's king, and White's queen is also aimed at d6.
student.why_not_alt: 1.Qc3 is too slow. Black plays 1...Qd5 and keeps the extra pawn, so White's queen is stuck guarding d6. White's king stays in the centre and Black's queen and rook keep swarming it.
student.plan: Bring the rook to c3, then use the c-file and queen against Black's king.

teacher.assessment: White is slightly better: more space and the active Nf5, while Black's f8-bishop is passive.
teacher.idea: Kick the f4 knight. Its best square, h3, is offside and vulnerable.
teacher.why_best: 1.g3 hits the knight. After 1...Nh3+ 2.Kg2 it sits on the rim, and Bc1 adds another attacker. It can end up short of squares. g3 also gives White's king a flight square.
teacher.why_not_alt: Re1 leaves the f4 knight unchallenged and the back rank unrelieved. Black regroups calmly with ...g6 and ...Qd7, and the game is equal.
teacher.plan: Hunt the h3 knight with Kg2 and Bc1, then use the queen's checks.

student.idea: Push g3 to hit the f4 knight and open the c1-bishop's diagonal.
student.assessment: White is slightly better: more space, Black's f4 knight is loose, and White's pieces are active.
student.why_best: 1.g3 attacks the f4 knight, so Black must defend it. After 1...Nh3+ 2.Kg2 the knight jumps to g2, and 3.Bc1 hits the c1-bishop. White's pieces then come in with ...Rd1 and ...Qb3+.
student.why_not_alt: 1.Re1 is too slow. Black plays 1...g6, develops with ...b5, and the f4 knight stays safe. White's pieces stay cramped and passive.
student.plan: Bring the rook to d1, the queen to b3, and the bishop to c1.

teacher.assessment: Black is a piece up, but White has real attacking chances against the exposed king and the weak f6-pawn.
teacher.idea: Bring the idle knight into the attack via g3–h5 before cashing in.
teacher.why_best: After 1.Ng3 the knight heads for h5, adding a third attacker on f6 with check. After 1...Rf7 2.Nh5+ Kf8 3.Nxf6, Black's king is stuck in the centre and White keeps enough pressure to hold the balance.
teacher.why_not_alt: 1.Qg3+ only drives the king into the corner. Then Bxf6 trades off White's best attackers, and in that simpler position Black's extra material starts to count.
teacher.plan: Pile up on f6 with knight, queen and bishop; keep the black king in the centre.

student.idea: Develop with tempo, not with checks, before Black's checks start.
student.assessment: Roughly equal. White's pieces are active, and Black's king is stuck in the centre.
student.why_best: Ng3 adds a second attacker to the f6 pawn and eyes the g7 king. It also frees the knight, so White can calmly go Nh5+ and Nxf6, winning the pawn.
student.why_not_alt: Qg3+ is a check that starts a tempo race. After Kh8, Qh4+ and Bxf6, White wins the f6 pawn, but Black's king escapes with Rxf6 and Qxf6, and White is left with no compensation.
student.plan: Win f6 with Nh5+, then use the knight and bishop to finish development.

teacher.assessment: White is slightly better with queen and extra pawn, but Black's two rooks can hold if they stay together.
teacher.idea: Bring the rook to the sixth rank to guard the king and stay compact.
teacher.why_best: After 1...Rg6 the rook covers the sixth rank, and 2.Qc5 Re6 builds a safe shelter around the king. The rooks protect each other, so the queen has no easy checks or targets.
teacher.why_not_alt: 1...Rd1+ is a check that achieves nothing. It splits the rooks, and after 2.Kg2 the queen starts checking (Qb8+, Qb4+, Qh4+) against Black's exposed king.
teacher.novel_concept: rooks defend each other vs queen
teacher.plan: Keep the rooks connected near the king, then use one to stop the a-pawn.

student.idea: Bring the rook to g6 to hit the queen and the king.
student.assessment: White is slightly better. Black's king is stuck in the centre, and White's queen and rooks are active.
student.why_best: Rg6 attacks the queen and the king. After 2.Qc5 Re6, the rook covers f7 and h7, so White's queen has no good squares. Black's rook then walks to a8 and stays active.
student.why_not_alt: Rd1+ is a check that leads nowhere. After 2.Kg2 Rg6, White's queen and rook are active, and White's king is safe. Black's rook is passive and loses time.
student.plan: Bring the rook to a8, then use the g-file and the king's pawns.

teacher.assessment: About equal after bxc6. Black is in danger now: White threatens Nc7 mate, and the c6 knight is a key attacker.
teacher.idea: Take the knight on c6 to stop mate and win back material.
teacher.why_best: The c6 knight attacks the rook on b8. It also covers d8 and e7, so Nc7 would be mate. After 1...bxc6 2.Rxc6 a6, Black frees the king and wins material back. The game levels out.
teacher.why_not_alt: 1...f6 gives the king a square but leaves the knight alive. After 2.Nxb8 White wins the exchange, keeps attacking, and ends up a lot of material ahead.
teacher.plan: Use ...a6 to drive off the b5 knight, then develop and get the king safe.

student.idea: Take the free knight on c6, then trade off White's rook and bishop.
student.assessment: Roughly equal. White is a pawn up, but Black's knight on d7 is attacked and can be taken.
student.why_best: The c6 knight is hanging. 1...bxc6 wins it outright. After 2.Rxc6 a6 3.Ba7 axb5, Black trades off White's best pieces, and the material is level.
student.why_not_alt: 1...f6 is a passive pawn break. It lets White play 2.Nxb8, winning the exchange, and Black's knight stays attacked. White is clearly winning.
student.plan: Trade off White's rook and bishop, then finish development and castle.

teacher.assessment: Black is up material, but White can win back a whole bishop and reach roughly equal chances.
teacher.idea: Take the loose bishop on d6. Nothing in Black's camp recaptures.
teacher.why_best: Black's queen can't defend d6 because the c6 pawn blocks her. So 1.Bxd6 wins a clean piece and cuts Black's lead from 6 to about 2. White also keeps the d6 bishop deep in Black's camp.
teacher.why_not_alt: 1.g6 ignores the free bishop. Black answers 1...Bxf4, swaps off the hanging piece and leaves White with doubled f-pawns, still clearly lost.
teacher.plan: Keep the d6 bishop strong, push g6 to loosen Black's king, then open the centre.

student.idea: Recapture with the bishop so the queenside pawns stay intact.
student.assessment: Roughly equal. White is a piece down, but Black's queenside pawns are doubled and Black's king is still in the centre.
student.why_best: 1.Bxd6 wins a piece and removes the bishop pair. After 1...Nd7 2.g6 f5 3.e4, White's queenside pawns are active and the game is level.
student.why_not_alt: 1.g6 gives up the bishop for a pawn. After 1...Bxf4 2.exf4 White has doubled pawns, but Black's king is safe and the game is lost.
student.plan: Play g6, e4, and use the queenside pawns and the d-pawn.

teacher.assessment: White is winning: the queen and rook on the eighth rank surround Black's bare king on g6.
teacher.idea: Take the king's escape squares with g4, then deliver checks to mate.
teacher.why_best: g4 covers h5 and f5, so the g6 king is boxed in. White threatens h5+ and Rg8+. After 1...Qa1+ 2.Kg2 Rc8 3.Rg8+ Kh7 4.Qxc8, White wins the rook and mate follows.
teacher.why_not_alt: e4 is still winning but lets the king out. Black's king can run to h5, and the e4 pawn falls to ...Qxe4. White wins material but gets no forced mate.
teacher.plan: Threaten h5+ and Rg8+ to drive the king into a mating net.

student.idea: Push g4 to open the c8–h4 diagonal toward Black's king.
student.assessment: White is winning. Black's king is stuck in the centre, and White's queen and rook are aimed at it.
student.why_best: 1.g4 opens the c8–h4 diagonal, so the queen and rook can hunt it. After 1...Qa1+ 2.Kg2 Rc8 3.Rg8+ Kh7 4.Qxc8 White wins the rook for a queen, and the attack continues.
student.why_not_alt: 1.e4 is too slow. Black gets time to regroup with ...Rd7 and ...Qxe4, and White's attack is gone.
student.plan: Bring the queen and rook to h7 and g8, then hunt the king.

teacher.assessment: Roughly equal, but Black is slightly better: White's isolated d4-pawn is a fixed target for Black's pieces.
teacher.idea: Pile up on the weak d4-pawn with knight and g7-bishop.
teacher.why_best: Nf5 joins the Bg7 in hitting d4, so White must push 2.d5. That gives up the d4 square, and after the rook trade the knight jumps to d4, a strong central post. Black also gets checking chances.
teacher.why_not_alt: Nc6 also hits d4, but the knight can simply be taken by Bxc6 after the rook trade. White stays central and the game fizzles to equal.
teacher.plan: Plant the knight on d4, then bring the queen to f5 against White's king.

student.idea: Jump to f5 to hit the e8 rook and the queen.
student.assessment: Roughly equal. Black's pieces are active, but White's rook on e8 is the main threat.
student.why_best: 1...Nf5 attacks the e8 rook, so White must answer with 2.d5. That opens the e-file toward Black's king. After 2...Rxe1+ 3.Qxe1 Nd4, Black's knight reaches the centre and the queen eyes the d-file.
student.why_not_alt: 1...Nc6 is slow. White plays 2.Rxe8+ Qxe8 3.Qe3, and Black's queen is stuck in the centre. White keeps the extra piece, and the position is roughly equal.
student.plan: Bring the knight to d4, then use queen and bishop checks against White's king.

teacher.assessment: White is better: active rook on d6, strong knight on b6, and Black's king stuck in the centre.
teacher.idea: Hit the b5 bishop while Black is busy with the d-file.
teacher.why_best: 1.c4 attacks the bishop on b5 while Black is still dealing with the d6 rook and d-file pressure. In the main line, after 1...Rxd6 2.exd6+ Kxd6 3.cxb5 axb5, White has won a piece for pawns.
teacher.why_not_alt: 1.Red1 only defends. Black gets time for 1...Bf4 and ...Bxe5, wins the e5 pawn, trades rooks and reaches a worse but holdable ending.
teacher.plan: Bring the extra piece into play, check with Rd1+ and go after Black's queenside pawns.

student.idea: Push the passed c-pawn to open the d6 rook and win it.
student.assessment: White is winning. The c-pawn is passed, and Black's king is stuck in the centre.
student.why_best: 1.c4 hits the b5 bishop, so Black must answer with 1...Rxd6. After 2.exd6+ Kxd6 3.cxb5 axb5, White has a passed pawn on c3. The rook on d6 also adds pressure.
student.why_not_alt: 1.Red1 is a slow regrouping move. It lets Black play 1...Bf4 and trade rooks, so White's edge shrinks to just a small one.
student.plan: Keep the extra passed c-pawn, then push the d-pawn and use the d6 rook.

teacher.assessment: Black is better. His rook, knight and f3-bishop all aim at White's boxed-in king, and the h3-pawn is weak.
teacher.idea: Remove the knight before it joins the attack, then activate the rook.
teacher.why_best: 1.Bxd5 cxd5 removes Black's best attacker and swaps off White's passive b3-bishop. Then 2.Rc3 attacks the f3-bishop, so White's rook gets active with tempo. Black wins h3, but White's king is much safer.
teacher.why_not_alt: 1.Kd2 lets Black take h3 with his knight still on the board. White ends up making the same trade later anyway, but with his rook pushed back to passive defence (Rg1, Re1).
teacher.plan: Activate the rook, keep the king safe, use the b2-bishop and the queenside space.

student.idea: Trade off Black's strong d5 knight before it lands on White's king.
student.assessment: Black is slightly better: White's king on e1 is exposed to Black's rook and bishop, and Black's pieces are active.
student.why_best: 1.Bxd5 cxd5 removes Black's best attacker. After 2.Rc3 Rxh3, White's king is stuck in the centre. White's pieces stay active, and Black's king is boxed in.
student.why_not_alt: 1.Kd2 lets Black play 1...Rxh3. White's king escapes with 2.Rg1, and Black's pieces get time to develop. White's king is safe, but Black's pieces are active.
student.plan: Play Rc3, then Bc1 to box in Black's king, and keep Black's pieces active.

teacher.assessment: Roughly equal. Black's extra pawn is offset by the pinned e7-bishop and an exposed king on the e-file.
teacher.idea: Seize the open d-file with tempo; the back-rank threat buys time to unpin.
teacher.why_best: 1...Rd8 takes the only open file and eyes White's weak back rank, so White spends a move on 2.Re1. That gains Black the time for ...Rd7, which guards e7 and loosens the pin on the bishop.
teacher.why_not_alt: 1...Rf8 is passive. It gives White a free hand, and after 2.Qg4 and 3.Rae1 White doubles rooks on the e-file against the pinned bishop.
teacher.plan: Play ...Rd7 to shield e7, tuck the king away, then use the extra pawn.

student.idea: Bring the rook to d8 to guard f6 and the king.
student.assessment: Roughly equal. Black is a pawn up, but White's rook on f6 and queen on e2 threaten to win f6.
student.why_best: Rd8 covers f6 and the king. After 2.Re1 Rd7 3.a3, Black's rook stays near the king, and the queen stays on c5 guarding d6. White's rook on f6 is only a small threat.
student.why_not_alt: Rf8 also guards f6, but it steps off the king. After 2.Qg4, White's queen and rook both hit d6, and Black's rook is no longer near the king.
student.plan: Keep the rook near the king, then use the queen and rook against White's pieces.
